messages:
alice_infra: Heads-up — noticed a spike in GPU job restarts during the 03:10 maintenance window. Looks like spot preemptions overlapped with CA-initiated drains and several jobs lost KV cache state.

bhavik_sre: saw the same. traces show kubelet started evict -> pod terminated before our cache flush hook completed. lots of tiny restarts, increased cost due to rework.

sara_platform: do we currently run any graceful termination handler on the GPU AMIs? I thought we had a termination-notice-daemonset but maybe it's not wired to our job runner.

maria_eng: we have a handler but it's only watching GCP preemptible metadata and has a 30s sync loop. not enough for long-running generates that need to checkpoint KV.

alice_infra: idea: extend the termination hook to emit a NodeCondition and taint the node with "spot/delayed-evict=true:NoSchedule" immediately, then let a small time window (configurable, 120s) for pods to flush. That would stop new pods being scheduled while giving more time for in-flight flush.

bhavik_sre: +1. also we should coordinate with cluster-autoscaler so it doesn't scale-down during that grace window. CA has scaleDownDelayAfterAdd, but we need a signal it respects. maybe use a node annotation like "cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true".

sara_platform: CA reads annotations but only in certain versions. which k8s + CA are we on?

maria_eng: running 1.25 + cluster-autoscaler 1.23. annotations supported. I can add a quick patch to termination handler to add that annotation and remove it after the grace period.

alice_infra: sample flow I'm proposing:
1) termination notice received -> add node taint: spot/preempting=yes:NoSchedule and annotation CA-disable
2) signal pods via preStop hook or a custom HTTP endpoint to flush KV/cache
3) once all flush signals ack or timeout (config default 2m) -> call kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
4) remove CA annotation and let CA/Cloud finish lifecycle

bhavik_sre: that sounds solid. two more asks: add a metric for "node_preempt_grace_taken_seconds" and emit a debug log with pod list on taint so we can triage which workloads didn't flush.

maria_eng: agreed. i'll add a prometheus metric and a compact log line like: "preempt_grace: node n returned pending: podA,podB".

sara_platform: also let's adjust pod specs for critical GPU jobs: add toleration for a custom taint "spot/delayed-evict" for a short window so they won't be immediately evicted, plus a preStop hook that POSTs to our /flush endpoint. example pod snippet:
```
livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /metrics
    port: 8080
preStop:
  exec:
    command: ["/bin/sh","-c","curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9000/flush || true; sleep 5"]
 tolerations:
  - key: "spot/delayed-evict"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoExecute"
    tolerationSeconds: 180
```

alice_infra: nice. also consider a nodePool-level config: dedicated warm-pool of preemptible GPUs with taint for low-priority jobs. That reduces impact on latency-sensitive production generators. warm-pool size = 10% of GPU capacity seemed effective in tests.

bhavik_sre: cost note: our spot pool is ~65% cheaper on avg, but rework and retries ate about 8% of that saving last week. If we reduce restarts by half we'll reclaim meaningful savings.

maria_eng: i'll push a PR for termination-handler + metrics + CA annotation by EOD. can someone write the runbook steps for on-call?

alice_infra: i'll draft the runbook: steps to check node taint, metrics, and force-drain if handler failed:
- check node: `kubectl get nodes -l cloud="gcp" -o wide`
- see taint: `kubectl describe node <node>` -> look for spot/preempting or spot/delayed-evict
- list pods: `kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>`
- if flush failed and pod is stuck >grace timeout: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --timeout=10m`
- escalate to infra if CA is not picking up annotated nodes (ticket template provided)

sara_platform: i'll add a snippet to redeploy job runner to include preStop and toleration changes. also will add integration test that simulates termination notice and asserts KV persisted.

ops_bot: incident detected: node-preempt-events spiked at 2025-07-14T03:10Z (+23 events). linked to thread https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-789

alice_infra: thanks. assign me INFRA-789 for the runbook + followups. can we schedule a quick sync tomorrow 09:30 PT to finalize values (grace window, tolerationSeconds, warm-pool %) ? :calendar: 

bhavik_sre: 👍 will be there. thanks all :thumbsup:

maria_eng: PR opened -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/402 (contains handler + metrics + CA annotation). requesting review from @bhavik_sre and @alice_infra.

sara_platform: adding integration test and will link. good progress.
